headline: Your takes survive the phone
lede: PLAICRAFT S6 gives consented recordings a durable outbox: a finished run is written to device storage before the first upload attempt, so an app that closes, backgrounds, or loses signal ships when the phone breathes again — and revoking consent wipes the queue instead of shipping it.

notes.text: The kill test is real: a consented Gauntlet run, the upload held open mid-flight, the browser killed — after relaunch the take arrives at the store, validates, and replay-verifies tick-for-tick against the sim. 20/20 gates (npm run plaicraft:outbox).

Privacy rule from the storage side: revoke motion consent and every queued take is purged from the device — nothing uploads AND nothing lingers. Permanent refusals (oversize, bad envelope) drop instead of clogging; dead stores quiet-retry at boot and on reconnect.
Gauntlet recordings now stamp the hero you picked — the seed never fixed it, so replays silently rebuilt the default warrior. The store's replay tools honor the stamp; old files keep working.

Filed #1793: first-consent Gauntlet runs sometimes diverge at a seed-invariant tick (~570) on replay — a wall-time float suspected inside hashed state. It threatens the 100% replay-verify line; fix before the phone-drive stage.
